:::{#hero-heading}

PhD Candidate in Applied Social and Health Psychology  
Colorado State University

### Making healthy behavior fit real life.

My research examines how health-promoting behaviors can fit into everyday life without creating unrealistic demands on people's time, attention, or routines. I focus primarily on physical activity and sedentary behavior, using workplace and everyday settings to study when movement is feasible, how people respond differently to the same intervention, and what supports sustained behavior change.

Across this work, I am especially interested in when, for whom, and under what conditions an intervention works. My research combines laboratory experiments with mixed-methods and field studies to understand both whether an intervention is effective and whether people can realistically use it.

:::

## Research

My research moves between controlled laboratory studies and real-world settings to examine how physical activity and other health behaviors can be integrated into daily life. Current work focuses on activity-permissive workstations, the timing of brief walking around acute stress, intervention heterogeneity, and longer-term movement use.

[Read more about my research](research.qmd)

## Teaching & Mentoring

My teaching and mentoring share the same basic goal: helping students move from guided practice toward independent thinking and ownership. In the classroom, I use active learning and scaffolded research projects; in the lab, students can progress from protocol training to project leadership, conference presentations, and manuscript involvement.
